top_cited_works.title: Transformation: From Teacher‐Centered to Student‐Centered Engineering Education
top_cited_works.abstract: Abstract We compare and contrast teacher‐centered and student‐centered paradigms of engineering education. We identify the following seven roles for teachers wishing to adopt a student‐centered paradigm: 1) model thinking/processing skills, 2) identify students' cognitive development, 3) develop questions that facilitate exploration/growth, 4) introduce visual tools to aid establishing connections, 5) provide group learning settings, 6) use analogies and metaphors, and 7) provide a “no‐risk” student feedback channel for information. Several case studies for different subjects and from different institutions are presented. Our results indicate a student‐centered model is most effective when coupled with academic depth and experience in the subject matter.

recent_works.title: Multispecies Justice in Engineering, and Engineering Design
recent_works.venue: Synthesis lectures on engineers, technology, and society
recent_works.abstract: A new ethical framework for the field of engineering, multispecies justice, has been developed. Multispecies justice in engineering advocates for broadening ethical responsibility to recognize nonhuman species as valid stakeholders in the design and execution of technological systems. This framework encourages engineers to evaluate the impact of their work on the welfare, agency, and ecological functions of animals, and to pursue design approaches that support coexistence, minimize harm, and advance equity among species. Rather than an appeal for compassion alone, it represents a systematic shift in how engineering defines its objectives, assesses success, and interprets its broader effects.
